name: Rekarina 1.2.9
body:
## Rekarina 1.2.9: buttons that follow your controller, and fixes for Radeon

Controls and buttons
- When you switch between keyboard and controller, texts already on screen change their buttons at once too, instead of keeping the old ones until they are shown again.
- Keyboard keys in the button pictures are readable: Shift is an arrow, and words like CTRL and TAB are bigger on a wider key.
- Sliders with fractional steps (gamma, walk speed, mouse sensitivity) move both ways with the keyboard and the controller again (thanks Zem).

Graphics
- The figures frozen in the ice should now hold still below 60 fps too (thanks OmniiOMEGA). If they still move for you, a short clip in #bug-reports helps.
- Radeon and other non-NVIDIA cards: textures chosen per pixel are now marked the way Vulkan requires. It may help the flicker and the crashes on RX 7000 and 9000 cards; that is not confirmed yet, so please tell us what you see (thanks Snowtime, Saito, BatzZie, JadsterNZ1 and k4k4shi).
- Radeon cards without float atomic add, like the RX 6600: values that some effects add up every frame were copied back over the game's own reset instead of being added to it. That is fixed, and it may be behind the white-out with black spots in parts of the forest; that is not confirmed yet (thanks the_artspear).
- V-Sync modes other than Mailbox no longer let the driver take the screen over in exclusive fullscreen, which should end the flash, the oversaturated colours and the odd alt-tab (thanks Arrant).

Crashes and starting
- With DLSS frame generation chosen in rekarina.ini, the game now starts on a Radeon or an integrated GPU too, and uses AMD's frame generation there.
- Radeon: when AMD's driver makes a colour image larger than the room the game gave it, that image now gets memory of its own, so the extra part no longer lies over the game's next texture. It may help the crashes on RX 7000 and 9000 cards and the Ally X that come seconds after a new area loads and the shield shining green or purple before them; that is not confirmed yet, so please tell us (thanks JadsterNZ1, k4k4shi and IDIR).
- AMD: the shader cache starts fresh by itself when it reaches the driver's size limit, so the game stops building the same shaders at every start (thanks JadsterNZ1 and Vireca).
- Opened straight from its folder, the game no longer keeps a console window, and the debug lines that filled it are gone from the log (thanks Mr Kat).

Setup and launcher
- The single Rekarina.exe unpacks itself without Windows' tar.exe, so folders with letters outside your Windows language work (thanks FrankE).
- When the shader step stops on a damaged game dump, the setup now names the damaged file in your .nup instead of showing a bare unpacking error (thanks fartnug).
- The launcher's line about FSR 1 says plainly that it only scales the finished picture up to a larger window, and that DLSS and frame generation are in the game's menu (thanks Post MaLune).
- The update from 1.2.8 only compiles the game's runtime again and redraws the button pictures: a few minutes, no shader translation.

Not ready yet
- Radeon RX 7000/9000: the sunlight flicker in the forest and some crashes are still being worked on; the test switches are in the Radeon thread in #bug-reports.
- Cards without mesh shaders (RX 400, 500 and 5000 series): missing walls and crashes.
- Memory on handhelds with shared memory (k4k4shi) and on 6 GB cards over long sessions (huchi001): fixes are written and being measured.
- HDR built on RenoDX's tone mapping, and sharper motion for DLSS on the hero's clothes: in the works.
- Flicker that still needs checking: the light on water and the reflections in the frozen domain.
- Depth of field still looks coarse at 1440p (Valentyn_L).
- The ghost portraits (Sable), FSR frame generation under Linux with RADV (Sabotage), the right stick moving the hero (fuo).
- Older processors are held back by recording each frame on the CPU; Linux and Steam Deck are not ready yet.

Something broken? Esc, Advanced, Make a problem report, and post the zip in #bug-reports.
